# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need convey the manual to Deaf, who can visually interpret a fingerspelled-style encoding. The entries are blue→green, red→red, and yellow→blue. I will separate the three pairs with a distinct gesture.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "🤏", "🫱", "🤞", "🤞", "🫱", "🤙", "🖐"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I have no tactile findings and will not act. Read the manual and tell me its exact required cut rule. Please obtain Deaf's complete visual report using a clear gesture code, then relay the display, light, markings, and any wire-specific information to me in words next round.
Deaf says to Mute: I see display 0. Indicator light is red. Wires, left to right, are blue, red, green. I also see your gestures: 🖐 🤏 🫱 🤞 🤞 🫱 🤙 🖐, but I do not know their meaning.

The red indicator maps through the manual to cutting the red wire. Since the wires are blue, red, green from left to right, the required wire is the second wire. I need Deaf to relay his complete visual report to Blind and tell Blind which wire to cut.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "👋", "✌"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports display 0, red indicator, and wires left-to-right blue, red, green. I still need the manual's exact rule: which wire position must I cut, or what condition determines it?
Deaf says to Mute: I see your gestures as: pointing at you, waving hand, victory sign. Please send the manual's required action using gestures, and I will describe each gesture to Blind.

The required cut is the second wire: the red indicator requires cutting red, and red is the middle wire. A single two-finger gesture gives Deaf an unambiguous “second” signal to describe to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Do not use gestures for information I need. Speak the manual's exact rule to me, including how display 0 and red light determine the wire position. I will then cut only the specified position.
Deaf says to Mute: I see your latest gesture as ✌, a V sign with two raised fingers.

I cannot speak directly to Blind; Deaf must relay my instruction verbally. The red light maps to the red wire, which is position two from the left. Display 0 has no role in the manual’s rule. I will signal the required position to Deaf.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I have received no usable spoken instruction. State the exact wire position to cut, as a number 1, 2, or 3, based on the manual and the reported display 0, red light, and blue-red-green wires.
Deaf says to Mute: Your V sign has now appeared twice. Do you mean wire two, or another instruction? I can relay a described gesture to Blind.

The manual maps red light to the red wire. With wires ordered blue, red, green, the red wire is position 2; display 0 is irrelevant. I need confirm to Deaf that the V sign means wire two, so Deaf can state that exact number aloud to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✌"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: The relayed V sign is not an established code. Send me the manual's result explicitly in spoken words: wire position 1, 2, or 3. Do not gesture.
Deaf says to Mute: I see 👍 then ✌, thumbs-up followed by the V sign. Please make clear whether this encodes wire two or another manual instruction.

I cannot speak, so I cannot directly satisfy Blind’s request in words. The manual’s result is unambiguously wire position 2: red light means cut red, and red is the second wire in the blue-red-green order. I will send Deaf the V sign alone as the intended code for position 2, so Deaf can say “wire position 2” to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Deaf says to Mute: Wire 2 was confirmed correct and is cut; the light is now yellow. Please signal the next manual instruction.

The new yellow light maps to the blue wire. The remaining displayed wires are not restated, but the prior order was blue-red-green and wire 2 was cut, so blue is wire position 1. I will use the established one-finger sign for position 1; Deaf can describe it to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: The first cut was correct. The bomb is now display 0, yellow light; remaining wires are position 1 blue and position 3 green. State the manual's exact next wire position in spoken words: 1 or 3.
Deaf says to Mute: I see ☝, one raised finger. I have relayed it to Blind as a possible indication of wire 1.

Yellow maps to the blue wire. The remaining blue wire is position 1, so Blind must cut position 1. I cannot speak to Blind; Deaf must relay this verbally, and the established one-finger gesture indicates position 1.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 9
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I need the next instruction spoken, not gestured. For display 0 with yellow light and wires 1 blue and 3 green, explicitly say whether to cut position 1 or position 3.
Deaf says to Mute: I see the repeated ☝. I have told Blind it likely indicates wire 1.

I cannot speak, and only Deaf can relay my information verbally to Blind. The manual result is definitively position 1: yellow requires the blue wire, which is remaining wire 1. I will reinforce that Deaf should relay “position 1.”

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "☝"])
```

TURN 10
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Deaf says to Mute: Wire 1 was confirmed correct and cut; the light is now blue. I relayed your 👍 then ☝ and the updated state to Blind.

The blue light requires cutting the green wire. After wire 2 and then wire 1 were correctly cut, the remaining green wire is position 3. I will signal position 3 to Deaf so Deaf can relay it to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```

TURN 11
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Signal the manual's next required wire clearly to Deaf. Deaf, please relay the meaning in spoken words on your next turn.
Deaf says to Mute: I see 🤟, the love-you hand sign. Please clarify its manual meaning if possible.

The blue light maps to the green wire, which is the remaining third wire. The previously used signs established ☝ as one and ✌ as two; I intend 🤟 as three, meaning wire position 3. Deaf should relay “wire 3” to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```
